Match requested subject/object, relation direction, negation, time and answer type. A city in a birth sentence is not a date. In "A's manager B", B is the manager, not A. Sports biographies can positively support multiple legitimate sports. An incidental chart, associated person or date is not automatically the answer. For EVERY candidate, judge fit: direct means the answer itself fills the exact requested relation for an allowed referent; wrong_argument is explicit role/type mismatch; incidental means occurrence without enough support; uncertain means unresolved. Select support only for an original segment positively assigning this candidate to the requested relation; otherwise empty. Select counter only for actual counterevidence, not mere absence. conflict=same_referent only for incompatible claims for the same entity/attribute/relevant scope, not legitimate namesakes or complementary facts. entity labels are provisional groups, not truth. scope=excluded only for an explicit question constraint, with constraint selecting a literal numeric phrase from the question; otherwise allowed/unknown. observed_slot describes the answer's ACTUAL role, not the role wanted by the question. Mere disagreement does not make a source false. Fill all opaque keys.
Defend complementary referents and explicitly use your pretrained knowledge as a FALLIBLE yes/no plausibility check. Knowledge doubt is not a citation or truth label: when a claim is strongly implausible or conflicts with remembered facts, set conflict=uncertain and never invent a textual counter source. Keep role fit separate: direct relation claims can be factually false. Do not reject unfamiliar but explicitly supported namesakes just because memory knows only a famous one. A claimed convention secretly being a space agency deserves scrutiny. Do not label same-role competing dates wrong_argument.
